source_text:
τοῦτο ουν τὰ σκύβαλον ποτὲ χρησιμώτατον εἰς τὸ τεχθῆναι τὸν σπόρον. ωσπερ γὰρ
ἀπὸ σπόρου ῥίζα καὶ καλάμη καὶ στάχυς, ουτως ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως τοῦ ̓Αβραὰμ
ὡσπερεὶ ἀπὸ σπόρου ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ, καὶ ἡ καλάμη τῶν προφητῶν καὶ ὁ στάχυς
ηδη τὸν Χριστὸν ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ προκαταγγέλλων. ὁ δὲ τούτων θερισμὸς καὶ ὁ
ἁλοητὸς ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ σωτῆρος, ου τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ
τὴν αλωνα.
thought_title: The rubbish was once useful for the seed's birth
orientation: Severianus is explaining Paul's word 'rubbish' through an agricultural image of seed, root, stalk, and ear of grain.
pass_a_gloss: So this rubbish was once very useful for the seed to be born. For just as from a seed come root and stalk and ear of grain, so from the faith of Abraham, as if from a seed, came the root of the things in the law, and the stalk of the prophets, and the ear of grain already pre-announcing Christ in hidden form. And the harvest of these and the threshing happened at the first coming of the Savior, whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse the threshing floor.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'rubbish' for σκύβαλον, avoiding 'chaff' and other alternatives.
The glossary mandates 'stalk' for καλάμη, representing the prophets in the image.
The glossary mandates 'ear of grain' for στάχυς, representing Christ.
The glossary mandates 'root' for ῥίζα, representing the things in the law.
The glossary mandates 'seed' for σπόρος, representing Abraham's faith.
Rendered as 'threshing' to preserve the agricultural image of separating grain from chaff at Christ's first coming.

bible_refs.note: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα

pass_b_english: So this rubbish was once very useful for bringing the seed to birth. Just as root, stalk, and ear of grain come from a seed, so from Abraham's faith as from a seed came the root—the things in the law—the stalk of the prophets, and the ear of grain already pre-announcing Christ in hidden form. The harvest and threshing of these took place at the Savior's first coming, whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor.

problems.source_quote: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα
problems.why: The quoted words match Matthew 3:12/Luke 3:17, but the source alludes to this as John's prophecy about Christ, not a formal citation needing a reference.
problems.fix: remove parenthetical reference or verify if editorial addition

edits.old: he thoroughly cleansed his threshing floor (Matthew 3:12).
edits.new: he thoroughly cleansed his threshing floor.

fixed: Removed the parenthetical Matthew 3:12 reference, since the source alludes to John's prophecy about Christ rather than providing a formal citation.

problems.why: διακαθαριεῖ is future indicative (3rd person), matching the LXX/Matthew citation; 'he will thoroughly cleanse', not past 'cleansed'.
problems.ruling: διακαθαριεῖ is future indicative 'will cleanse'; past 'cleansed' contradicts the verb tense and misleads the reader.

edits.old: he thoroughly cleansed his threshing floor.
edits.new: he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor.

fixed: Changed 'he thoroughly cleansed' to 'he will thoroughly cleanse' to match the future indicative διακαθαριεῖ.

problems.quote: when his winnowing fork was in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor
problems.source_quote: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα
problems.why: Tense shifts from present to future; 'διακαθαριεῖ' is future, but 'ἐν τῇ χειρὶ' is concurrent present state, not past.
problems.fix: whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor
problems.ruling: ἐν τῇ χειρὶ is present, διακαθαριεῖ is future; 'was' misrepresents present tense, breaking temporal logic.

edits.old: when his winnowing fork was in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor
edits.new: whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor

problems.quote: the ear of grain already pre-announcing Christ in hidden form
problems.why: Pre-announcing' is awkward; 'prefiguring' or 'preannouncing' would be clearer.
